query: Why do handling times differ by channel and priority?

per_column.name: issue_complexity
per_column.rationale: A complexity categorization is a genuine new axis that plausibly explains handling-time differences beyond the existing priority/channel fields, directly serving the query. However, groundedness is shaky: labels are only partially warranted by text. The invoice duplicate (CS-0001) is a fairly simple billing correction yet is rated High, while the 502 outage RCA (CS-0003) is Medium and the BOM/pipeline issue (CS-0005) is Low despite clear technical depth. These inconsistencies show the values are not reliably derived from source content.

per_column.name: urgency_factor
per_column.rationale: Urgency is analytically relevant to handling time, but it overlaps heavily with the existing 'priority' column, reducing its leverage. Groundedness is weak in places: the feature-request enhancement (CS-0004) is explicitly a small, non-urgent 'would value' item yet is labeled 'Blocking', contradicting the text, while genuine outages are also 'Blocking'. The category assignments are inconsistently supported.

per_column.name: channel_communication_mode
per_column.rationale: Mapping channel to Async/Sync is directly useful for the query since it reframes channel in terms of interaction latency, a plausible driver of handling time. But the values appear invented: the source_text samples expose only issue_description and lack any channel field, and the descriptions themselves give no basis for Sync vs Async. The Sync/Async labels are asserted without derivable evidence in the provided rows.

judge.rationale: All three columns offer plausible new axes (complexity, urgency, communication mode) relevant to explaining handling-time variation, though urgency partly duplicates the existing priority column. The main weakness is groundedness: several produced values are inconsistent with or unsupported by the source text (e.g., a simple invoice fix rated High complexity, a small enhancement labeled Blocking), and the Sync/Async mode has no visible evidence in the sampled rows. Values read as confident labels beyond what the text warrants.
